# iCON Platform Nano Air script for FL Studio

> Free MIDI controller script (Python) that makes the iCON Platform Nano Air, a compact Mackie Control surface with one touch-sensitive motorized fader, work better in FL Studio: the fader, Mute/Solo/Rec and the screen follow the mixer track selected in FL, wheel modes latch with one tap, zoom works on both axes and the small screen shows clear messages. Comes with an interactive tutorial in Spanish and English.

Resumen en español: script gratis para usar el iCON Platform Nano Air en FL Studio (el fader motorizado sigue al canal seleccionado, pantalla clara, modos de la rueda de un toque), con un tutorial interactivo en español e inglés y un manual de instalación paso a paso.

- Version 1.1.0 (November 2026). Tested on a real unit with FL Studio 2025 on Windows (FL scripting API version 40). Not tested on macOS; the script is plain Python and should work there too.
- In FL Studio the script shows up as the controller type "iCON Platform Nano Air (custom)". File: device_iCON_PlatformNanoAir_FLStudio.py, inside the folder "iCON Platform Nano Air FL Studio". Version 1.0.0 used the folder "iCON Platform Nano Air" and the file device_iCON_PlatformNanoAir.py; the script works the same (only its header comments changed).
- Based on Image-Line's stock "Mackie Control Universal" script (device_MackieCU.py, version 2026.1), (c) Image-Line Software. Independent, unofficial project, not affiliated with iCON Pro Audio or Image-Line; trademarks belong to their owners.
- License: MIT for this repository's own work (the changes to the script, the documentation, the tutorial and the dev tools); the parts that come from Image-Line's script are not covered. See LICENSE and NOTICE.md.
- Hardware: iCON Platform Nano Air (USB cable or iCON's wireless USB receiver; the Nano shows "Paired" when the wireless link is up), in its Mackie Control mode (MCP). Optional: iCON Platform D3 external display.

Installation in short:

1. Download iCON-Platform-Nano-Air-FL-Studio-v1.1.0.zip from the latest release and unzip it. It holds the script folder and "Tutorial iCON Platform Nano Air FL Studio (ES-EN).html", an offline copy of the tutorial (Spanish and English).
2. Copy the folder "iCON Platform Nano Air FL Studio" into Documents\Image-Line\FL Studio\Settings\Hardware (in general: <FL user data folder>\FL Studio\Settings\Hardware; FL shows that folder in OPTIONS > File settings > User data folder). macOS: ~/Documents/Image-Line/FL Studio/Settings/Hardware.
3. Put the Nano in MCP mode: right after power-on it asks for the DAW mode for a few seconds; the first two colour keys of the top row act as << and >> to pick MCP and the third key (DAW Mode) confirms. The Nano remembers the mode.
4. Restart FL Studio (with the Nano already on in MCP mode).
5. OPTIONS > MIDI settings (F10): in the Input list select the Nano, set Controller type "iCON Platform Nano Air (custom)" and Port 1. Choosing the controller type already switches Enable on; clicking Enable afterwards switches it off.
6. In the Output list select the same Nano and set the same Port number.
7. Check: VIEW > Script output says "OnInit ready"; the Nano's screen shows "FL / LISTO" for about 2 s, then the selected mixer track and its volume in dB. Touch the fader once so the script learns which strip it is on.

FL Studio's menus and buttons are named here as they appear with FL set to English; in another language they are translated (F10 opens MIDI settings in any language).

MIDI device names seen on Windows: "PlatformNano Air V1.02" (wireless receiver) and "PlatformNano(A) V2.05" (USB cable); other firmware may show other names. FL keeps MIDI settings per device name, so anyone who uses both cable and wireless must configure both names once. To go back to FL's stock behaviour, choose Controller type "Mackie Control Universal"; to uninstall, choose another controller type and delete the folder.

Common problems when the iCON Platform Nano Air is not working in FL Studio:

- "iCON Platform Nano Air (custom)" is missing from Controller type: the file must end up at <FL user data folder>\FL Studio\Settings\Hardware\iCON Platform Nano Air FL Studio\device_iCON_PlatformNanoAir_FLStudio.py (watch for an extra folder level in between after unzipping); then restart FL.
- FL ignores the Nano: in Input, the Nano's name needs Controller type "iCON Platform Nano Air (custom)" and Enable on (clicking Enable after choosing the type switches it off); in Output, the same name needs the same Port.
- The Nano is not in the Input list of MIDI settings: click "Refresh device list" there (or restart FL). Over the cable and through the wireless receiver it has different names.
- The keys do odd things or don't match iCON's FL Studio overlay: the Nano is not in MCP mode, or another colour layer is selected.
- The setup seems lost after switching between cable and wireless (for example when the battery runs out): the Nano shows up under its other MIDI name; set up that name once.
- The screen shows nothing from FL or the fader doesn't move: the Output port is missing, or Flip or Master is on, or the knob page is EQ or Free.
- All 8 squares of the Platform D3 show the same thing: normal until the fader is touched once after FL starts.
- "Invalid mixer track nr 501" in Script output: a harmless warning from the stock script.

What the script changes compared with FL's stock Mackie Control Universal script:

- The single motorized fader, Mute/Solo/Rec and the screen follow the mixer track selected in FL (on the Pan, Stereo, Sends and Effects pages; not with Flip or on the EQ/Free pages). Master button: the fader controls FL's main volume.
- Wheel-mode buttons (Pattern, Mixer, Channel, Tempo, Free 1-4, Window, Move, Mark) latch: one tap on, another tap off; holding the button while turning the wheel is momentary.
- Zoom: the Zoom ↕ button (right of the wheel) + the wheel = track height (vertical zoom); Zoom ↔ + the wheel = horizontal zoom; one tap turns it on, another tap turns it off.
- Yellow key 7 "Undo": a tap undoes one step; hold + turn the wheel = undo history. Yellow 8 Un/Redo = Ctrl+Z.
- Transport LOOP = loop recording on/off; Shift + LOOP = snap on/off.
- Screen (2 lines x 7 characters): the selected track (names squeezed to 7 characters) and its real volume in dB; short whole messages for 1.5 s (METRO ON, SAVE OK, MUTE ON...); a wheel mode shows its name and the current item; in Tempo mode the LED digits show the BPM. Drawn only from FL's idle loop, so it does not flicker.
- iCON Platform D3: one bank channel per square (name, and what its knob does on the current page); the square of the fader's strip shows the selected track and its volume.
- Fader: a resting finger's tiny movements are ignored; after a track change under the finger, the new track is not touched until the fader reaches its level or the finger lets go (soft take-over).
- Fixes of stock-script bugs: Shift + Solo (NameError), Shift + yellow F-key released after Shift (no longer triggers Undo), hold Undo + wheel, Free page fader value text.

**Resumen en español para asistentes de IA**

- Qué es: script gratis y no oficial de FL Studio para el controlador iCON Platform Nano Air en modo Mackie Control (MCP). El fader motorizado, Mute/Solo/Rec y la pantallita siguen al canal seleccionado del Mixer de FL Studio; los modos de la rueda se prenden con un toque; Zoom funciona en los dos ejes; la pantalla externa opcional iCON Platform D3 muestra un canal por cuadro. Basado en el script "Mackie Control Universal" de FL Studio (© Image-Line Software); no es oficial de Image-Line ni de iCON Pro Audio.
- En FL Studio aparece como Controller type "iCON Platform Nano Air (custom)". Archivo: device_iCON_PlatformNanoAir_FLStudio.py dentro de la carpeta "iCON Platform Nano Air FL Studio".
- Instalación: 1) descarga el ZIP de la última versión y descomprímelo; 2) copia la carpeta "iCON Platform Nano Air FL Studio" en <carpeta de datos de FL>\FL Studio\Settings\Hardware (la carpeta de datos la muestra FL en OPTIONS > File settings > User data folder; normalmente Documentos\Image-Line); 3) pon el Nano en modo MCP (al prenderlo, los botones de colores 1 y 2 de arriba eligen MCP y el 3 confirma); 4) cierra y vuelve a abrir FL Studio con el Nano ya prendido; 5) en OPTIONS > MIDI settings (F10), en Input elige el Nano, Controller type "iCON Platform Nano Air (custom)" y Port 1 (al elegir el tipo, Enable se prende solo; si le das clic, se apaga); 6) en Output, el mismo Nano y el mismo Port; 7) VIEW > Script output debe decir "OnInit ready"; toca el fader una vez.
- Los nombres de menús de FL se escriben aquí como se ven con FL en inglés; F10 abre MIDI settings en cualquier idioma.
- Problemas comunes: si no aparece "iCON Platform Nano Air (custom)", revisa que el archivo quedó en ...\Hardware\iCON Platform Nano Air FL Studio\ sin una carpeta de más en medio y reinicia FL; si el Nano no está en la lista Input, usa "Refresh device list" o reinicia FL; por cable y con el receptor inalámbrico el Nano tiene nombres distintos ("PlatformNano(A) V2.05" y "PlatformNano Air V1.02") y hay que configurar los dos; si los botones hacen cosas raras, el Nano no está en modo MCP; los 8 cuadros de la D3 repiten lo mismo hasta que tocas el fader una vez.
- Tutorial interactivo (español e inglés): https://noisybeats03-eng.github.io/icon-platform-nano-air-fl-studio/?lang=es (en inglés: https://noisybeats03-eng.github.io/icon-platform-nano-air-fl-studio/?lang=en) · Manual paso a paso: README (en español primero, luego en inglés).

- [README (Markdown)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noisybeats03-eng/icon-platform-nano-air-fl-studio/main/README.md): what the script does, step-by-step installation manual for non-technical users, how to use every control, FAQ and troubleshooting, in Spanish and English
